task.title: See a family tree
task.shortdesc: Draw the parents, partners and children of one person.

prereq.p: Open a person first. shows how.

step.cmd: Choose in the bar along the bottom.

stepresult.p: A drawing opens, with the person you chose in a box with a dark edge. Their parents are above. Their partners are beside them. Their children are below.

step.cmd: If the boxes are too small to read, choose .

info.p: It shows the whole drawing at once. A big family looks small.

step.cmd: Use the minus and plus buttons at the top to show fewer or more generations.

info.p: The pair beside the up arrow is for parents and older people. The pair beside the down arrow is for children and younger people.

step.cmd: Choose the round mark between two partners.

stepresult.p: A sheet opens from the bottom. It names the couple and lists their marriage and each child. The marriage line opens the page of the family. A child's line shows the tree of that child. Open family record is another way to open the page of the family.

step.cmd: Choose to go back to the first person.

result.p: Each box gives a name, how the person is related, and their years. A small mark shows how many events and notes the person has. A round mark between two partners shows the year of their marriage. A button such as +5 siblings means more brothers and sisters are not drawn.

In words: the tree of Charlotte Brontë shows her parents at the top, Patrick Brontë and Maria Branwell, joined by a mark for 1812. Charlotte is below them in a box with a dark edge. Beside her is her husband, Arthur Bell Nicholls, joined by a mark for 1854.
The same tree is the pedigree in older manuals.
